newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Allianz-BGZ expects losses at start.
newsitem.headline: Polish Allianz-BGZ expects losses at start.

text.p: Polish life and non-life insurer Allianz-BGZ SA, which launched operations in Poland, expects losses in the first several years, a member of Germany's Allianz AG management board said on Thursday.

Detlev Bremkamp told a news conference the losses would be incurred by making initial reserves and training staff but said he expected the Polish non-life unit to break even in the next few years and the life business in up to 10 years.

"We will have losses in both kinds of business in the next couple of years...in non-life hopefully we will achieve a break even in a couple of years and in the life...it will take five to ten years," he said.

Both non-life Allianz BGZ Polska SA and life Allianz BGZ Polska Zycie SA are 51-percent controlled by Poland's Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA and 49-percent by Germany's Allianz AG Holding and have 14 million zlotys in capital each.
Brigitte Bovermann, the president of both Polish-German insurers, also present, said the first non-life policies have already been sold and life insurance sales would likely start this summer.

"We have already issued the first policies for industrial and commercial clients and in the next three months we will start sales for households, the sale of life policies will start in summer," she said.
